findings.reason: The protected Python solution counts distinct nonempty substrings using a Suffix Automaton (SAM). It builds states, transitions, suffix links, and longest path lengths online in O(n) time. The distinct substring count is obtained by summing longest[state] - longest[suffix_link[state]] across all non-initial states. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(n) space, fully satisfying the problem's O(n) follow-up requirement; no candidate is required.

Suffix Automaton construction guarantees that each equivalence class of substrings corresponds to a unique state, and the length interval longest[v] - longest[suffix_link[v]] partitions all distinct substrings of s without duplicates.

Building a Suffix Automaton for a string of length n creates at most 2n - 1 states with amortized O(n) transition updates for a fixed 26-character alphabet, giving O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts string s and returns the total integer count of distinct nonempty contiguous substrings.

The approach accurately details Suffix Automaton construction, state cloning, suffix link maintenance, length interval summation, O(n) follow-up satisfaction, and O(n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover substring set hashing slice overheads, suffix trie quadratic memory limits, suffix array LCP subtraction methods, rolling hash collision risks, single-character base cases, all-identical-character linearly bounded outcomes, and position-independent deduplication.
